data.title: Is an Intel N100 or N150 a better value than a Raspberry Pi?
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary:
这篇文章比较了Intel N100迷你电脑和Raspberry Pi 5的性价比。作者一年前购买了GMKtec N100 NucBox G3，并与Raspberry Pi 5 8GB进行对比。如今，新款16GB N150迷你电脑和16GB Raspberry Pi 5发布，作者重新进行了基准测试，并在迷你电脑上安装了Linux以进行公平比较。

结果显示，即使配备较慢的DDR4内存的N100系统在性能上仍优于Raspberry Pi 5，但Raspberry Pi 5在能效方面表现更好。N100（或N150）的实际表现取决于其搭配的RAM、IO和散热方案。

二手迷你电脑价格更低，但新机的性价比取决于具体配置。Raspberry Pi 5更紧凑且在空闲时更省电，适合需要PoE供电的场景。Intel系统则更适合桌面使用，兼容更多软件，尤其是需要Windows的程序。

总体而言，选择取决于具体需求和使用场景，性价比并不简单直接可比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：N100与Raspberry Pi（及其他ARM单板计算机）在各种使用场景中的对比，包括性能、功耗、价格和可扩展性。

不同观点：
• **N100性价比更高，适合服务器和自托管项目**：whywhywhywhy和stego-tech等用户认为N100在作为Jellyfin服务器、种子下载器等任务中表现优异，且性价比高于Raspberry Pi。他们强调N100在完成任务和价格方面的优势，尤其是在不需要GPIO的情况下。

• **Raspberry Pi在功耗和GPIO扩展方面有优势**：poulpy123和firesteelrain指出，Raspberry Pi等ARM设备在功耗方面表现更好，适合需要低功耗的场景。此外，Raspberry Pi的GPIO接口使其在特定硬件项目（如PicoBalloon、OctoPrint等）中不可替代。

• **ARM的软件生态和乐趣**：Venn1和Havoc认为，虽然Raspberry Pi的软件编译和设置可能比较麻烦，但其软件生态和DIY乐趣是x86设备无法比拟的。同时，Raspberry Pi在一些特定应用中仍然具有优势。

• **N100在扩展性和稳定性上有优势**：voxadam和LikeBeans提到，N100 mini PC在存储和内存扩展性方面表现更好，且不需要使用SD卡等易损坏的存储介质。此外，N100设备在运行需要高吞吐量的任务（如防火墙、VPN等）时表现更佳。

• **N100设备的驱动和BIOS问题**：qingcharles和transpute指出，N100设备的驱动支持和BIOS更新可能存在问题，特别是来自第三方OEM的产品，这可能影响其长期使用的可靠性。

补充讨论：
• **具体使用场景决定选择**：多个评论提到，选择N100还是Raspberry Pi应根据具体使用场景决定。例如，Raspberry Pi适合低功耗和GPIO需求的项目，而N100更适合需要高性能和扩展性的任务。

• **市场价格和供货情况**：poulpy123和stego-tech提到，N100设备在某些市场（如AliExpress）上的价格优势明显，但需要注意供货和驱动支持问题。

• **个人偏好和体验**：hollerith和glimshe分享了他们的个人使用体验，认为N100在静音和性能方面满足了他们的需求，并表示不再使用Raspberry Pi。

争议焦点：
• **功耗与性能的权衡**：N100在性能和扩展性上占优，但功耗较高；Raspberry Pi则在功耗和GPIO扩展方面有优势。用户需根据具体需求权衡选择。

• **驱动和BIOS支持问题**：N100设备的驱动和BIOS更新问题引起了一些用户的担忧，特别是在长期使用和系统重装时可能遇到困难。

44463813.article_content:
Is an Intel N100 a better value than a Raspberry Pi?
tl;dr
:
it depends
.
About one year ago, I bought an Intel N100 mini PC (specifically the
GMKtec N100 NucBox G3
) and
compared it to the Raspberry Pi 5 8GB
.
A year later, and we have
a newer $159 16GB version of that mini PC
with a slightly-faster Intel N150, and a new
16GB Raspberry Pi 5
.
I re-ran all my benchmarks, and
this time
compared like-for-like, installing Linux on the Mini PC. Many people argued comparing the OOTB experience running Windows 11 Pro (which came on the Tiny PC) to Raspberry Pi OS (which I installed on the Raspberry Pi 5) was unfair.
I have a video that goes through everything in this post, embedded below:
If you prefer to read the post instead, please continue:
N100 PCs are not created equal
In the video, I ran through four myths to test whether they hold water—one of the most difficult to assess is whether the N100 is
faster
and
more efficient
than a Pi 5.
Because unlike the Pi, an N100 (or the newer N150) is just the SoC used on dozens (maybe
hundreds
now?) of boards, from prebuilt Tiny PCs to full-on motherboards. Manufacturers pair the SoC with different types of RAM, IO, and cooling options.
All that to say, if you're comparing an N100 paired with slow DDR4 RAM and a weak laptop fan to one running fast DDR5 RAM with a huge desktop CPU cooler, you're going to have a pretty different experience.
But even the slower DDR4-based systems beat the Pi 5 in raw performance, in my testing.
How much
depends a lot on the thermals and power limits.
On the NucBox G3, with DDR4 RAM and some thermal constraints which required me to pop the top off and place a fan over the back side of the main board, it was between 1.5-2x faster than a Pi 5, depending on the benchmark.
For example, High Performance Linpack saw almost double the performance:
But note the
efficiency
scores. Despite the N150 using 'Intel 7' (a 10 nm process node), it gets less work done per watt than the Pi 5 (whose Arm BCM2712 chip uses a 16nm process). So the maxim of "better process node == better efficiency" does
not
apply universally (not to mention comparing different process nodes is a fun experiment these days, because 1nm can mean a lot of different things!).
Architecture, feature sets, and chip design still matters.
I have
all
the dozens of benchmark results (and a log of the full process getting them) for both computers on my
SBC Reviews website
.
Used Tiny PCs are Cheaper
In news that should be obvious to anyone who thinks about it for more than half a second:
used Tiny PCs are cheaper
. Cheaper than both new fully-kitted-out Raspberry Pi 5s, and cheaper than new Tiny PCs.
Because of the massive quantity of leased Tiny/Mini/Micro PCs for business use (every doctor's office and hospital on the planet seems to have a dozen), there's a constant churn of 3-5 year old models, and many end up on eBay.
I acquired a couple old Lenovos this way, with 7th and 8th-gen Intel CPUs. Even though they burn a few more watts at idle, they're an excellent deal if you just need a little PC to run something in a homelab, or for a lightweight desktop.
They usually have more expansion options than a cheap Tiny PC or Pi have.
But newsflash:
used is different than new
. Just like used gaming consoles are cheaper than new ones... you can't say "Tiny PCs are cheaper than Raspberry Pis" based on
used
pricing versus
new
.
It's enough to say Tiny PCs are cheaper than Raspberry Pis if comparing
like for like
specs on
new
machines:
The Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB model, with 512 GB of SSD storage, Raspberry Pi's NVMe HAT, an Active Cooler, an RTC battery, a 27W power adapter, and a rubber bumper case, costs $208, compared to the similarly-specced GMKtec NucBox G3 Plus.
But you can't find a new fully-kitted Tiny PC in the $60-80 range that competes with the Pi 5, which starts at $50 for the bare Pi 5 board (for a 2 GB model). The most direct comparison is the Radxa X4 (which is a very close Intel-based replacement for the Raspberry Pi). But that board's pricing is very closely aligned to the Pi, as you need to add on accessories to have a fully functional system.
All of this to say: value is complicated. The Pi 5 is
much
more compact and slightly more power efficient (especially at idle) compared to the cheapest N1XX Intel systems. The Intel systems are better suited for a desktop use case. The Pi 5 can be run off PoE power, for easier one-cable networking + power. The Intel systems are more compatible with a wider range of software (not the least of which is
anything requiring Windows
).
The idle power is the difference of maybe $10-20/year of power consumption. So it's not
that big a deal
for most users. But it's substantial if you're running off PoE power for remote use cases, or need to run a computer off solar or battery power.
It's not that useful to say one is cheaper than the other, because it's like saying "a bicycle is cheaper than a car." If you need to transport 4 adults 150 miles as quickly

主要讨论点：对文章《bookofjoe》链接内容的评论分析，主要围绕信息的真实性、新闻的价值以及对媒体动机的质疑。

不同观点：
• 观点一：认为文章内容真实可信，强调其揭示了社会中被忽视的问题。有评论举例指出，过去类似的报道也揭露了许多鲜为人知的事实，表明这种深入调查具有社会价值。

• 观点二：质疑文章的真实性和动机，认为文章可能是为了吸引眼球或制造轰动效应。有评论指出，文章缺乏可靠的数据支持，且作者有夸大其词的历史，因此对文章的结论保持怀疑态度。

• 观点三：中立态度，认为文章提出了一些有趣的观点，但需要更多的证据来验证其真实性。有评论建议读者保持批判性思维，不要盲目相信单一信息来源，而应寻找更多的佐证材料。

• 观点四：批评媒体选择报道此类题材的动机，认为媒体更关注流量而非新闻的真实性和社会责任。有评论举例说，某些媒体倾向于报道有争议的话题以增加点击率，而不是关注重要的社会议题。

data.title: ICEBlock, an app for anonymously reporting ICE sightings, goes viral
data.author: exiguus
data.article_summary: ICEBlock是一款允许用户匿名报告美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）行踪的iPhone应用，在美国迅速走红。特别是在美国总检察长帕姆·邦迪批评该应用后，其下载量激增，成为美国App Store最受欢迎的免费应用之一。该应用用户主要集中在洛杉矶，用户可以在5英里范围内分享ICE行踪，并接收附近ICE sightings的通知。TechCrunch确认该应用不收集或存储任何用户数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于报告和规避警察活动的应用程序（ICEBlock）的合法性、隐私性、安全性及其社会影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持应用程序的观点**：
  - 用户有权选择避开警察活动，以避免不必要的麻烦，例如DUI检查或交通堵塞（neither_color）。
  - 该应用程序与Waze或汽车闪灯提醒其他司机有警察在附近的行为类似，属于言论自由的范畴，且多次法院判决支持这种行为的合法性（datax2）。
  - 执法人员应受到更高的监督和透明度，包括公开数据库和面部识别技术（jjwiseman）。
  - 该应用程序的存在本身反映了美国当前的社会问题，即需要此类工具来保护公民隐私（csto12）。

• **对应用程序合法性和隐私性的质疑**：
  - 担心应用程序可能被用于帮助犯罪分子逃避法律，且有人认为报道这些行为的文章也是在危害执法人员的安全（abeppu）。
  - 对应用程序的安全性和数据隐私保护的担忧，特别是Android版本的隐私问题（ldoughty, josefresco）。
  - 有人质疑苹果允许该应用程序上架的双重标准，因其曾拒绝过有关美国无人机袭击的应用程序（callahad）。

• **对政府和执法机构行为的批评**：
  - 批评政府官员公开威胁应用程序开发者的行为，认为这是滥用权力的表现（beepbopboopp, mikestew）。
  - 有人讽刺地将该应用程序与伊朗的类似应用相比较，暗示美国也在采取类似的监控措施（nottorp）。

补充讨论：
• **应用程序的技术实现**：
  - 讨论了应用程序的技术安全性，尤其是其不收集用户数据和网络流量的安全性（VladVladikoff）。
  - 有人质疑为什么该应用程序不是优先考虑隐私的PWA（渐进式网络应用程序），而是原生iOS应用（josefresco）。

• **应用程序的社会影响和政治背景**：
  - 有人认为ICE（美国移民和海关执法局）浪费纳税人的钱，应该将资源用于更有意义的公共服务（wnevets）。
  - 该应用程序引发的讨论可能会上升到最高法院，涉及第一修正案的保护范围（1970-01-01）。
  - 有人指出该应用程序的讨论热度部分源于对手战术的虚假报告（ramoz）。

争议焦点：
- 该应用程序是否属于言论自由的范畴，还是可能危害执法人员的安全。
- 政府和执法机构对应用程序开发者的公开威胁是否适当。
- 应用程序的隐私保护和安全性是否足够，特别是在不同平台上的处理差异。

In Brief
Posted:

Image Credits:
Christopher Dilts / Bloomberg / Getty Images
Zack Whittaker
ICEBlock, an app for anonymously reporting ICE sightings, goes viral overnight after Bondi criticism
ICEBlock, an iPhone app that allows users to anonymously report sightings of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents, has rocketed to one of the coveted top spots in Apple’s U.S. App Store rankings. The upshot: Criticism from U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi
helped get it there
.
Most of ICEBlock’s users — about 20,000 — were in Los Angeles, where
ICE raids have become commonplace
over recent weeks,
according to CNN
. Following Bondi’s remarks late Monday, the app went viral overnight. As of Tuesday afternoon, the app is now one of the most downloaded free iPhone apps in the United States.
With ICEBlock, users can lawfully share information about where they have seen ICE within a 5-mile radius of their location. The app also sends notifications when ICE agents are sighted near the user’s location.
The app does not collect or store any user data, which TechCrunch confirmed by analyzing the app’s network traffic as part of a test.

data.title: Atomic "Bomb" Ring from KiX (1947)
data.author: gscott
data.article_summary: 1947年，General Mills的KiX麦片品牌推出了一款原子“炸弹”戒指，顾客可用15美分加一个麦片盒顶换购。这款戒指又称“孤胆骑警原子炸弹戒指”，反映了当时公众对原子能的关注。戒指有可调节的金色带子，侧面有闪电爆炸图案，铝制弹头上有可拆卸的红色塑料尾翼，尾翼内可藏小秘密。移开红色底座后，可通过塑料镜头观察到闪光，这是由戒指内放射性同位素相互作用产生的，当时广告称其“完全安全”。由于所含的钋-210半衰期为140天，现存的这种戒指已无法产生可见闪光。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Radium和Polonium等放射性物质在消费品中的历史使用及其危险性

不同观点：
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为Radium手表是危险的，但基于其在非洲成长的经历，对某些潜在危险环境有较高的容忍度。他指出，尽管接触过如黑曼巴蛇等危险生物，自己还是存活下来，暗示对某些危险环境的适应性。
• [SoftTalker] 对Polonium-210的危害表示严重关切，引用维基百科的信息强调其高度放射性和对人体极端危险，并提到其易于空气传播。同时，提出质疑，有多少孩子可能摄入了这种物质，并联想到用Polonium-210进行的政治谋杀事件。
• [allenrb] 持怀旧态度，认为现代产品缺乏过去的品质，隐含对过去某些产品的肯定，但未具体讨论其安全性。
• [victor22] 对产品中是否真的含有放射性物质表示怀疑，暗示可能存在夸张或虚构成分。
• [foxglacier] 从更广泛的社会文化角度分析，认为上世纪的技术和未来憧憬令人兴奋，而当前尽管技术进步仍在继续，社会情绪却更加负面，并将此归因于气候变化带来的负面文化影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Polonium-210等放射性物质在消费品中的使用及其实际危害程度。一部分人对其危险性表示严重关切，另一部分人则对其存在与否或实际影响持怀疑态度。
• 不同评论者对历史产品的态度存在差异，有人基于个人经历淡化危险，有人则通过引用科学资料强调潜在风险。
• 社会文化背景和时代情绪的变化也被引入讨论，作为理解现代与过去对技术进步态度差异的一个视角。

44447797.article_content:
Release date:
1947 |
Where to purchase:
eBay
“It’s a seething scientific sensation!”
In 1947, General Mills’ KiX cereal brand offered the Atomic “Bomb” Ring as a premium in exchange for 15 cents plus a cereal box top. Also known as the Lone Ranger Atomic Bomb Ring, it was a reflection of the public’s preoccupation with the power and potential of atomic energy at the time.
The ring had an adjustable gold-coloured band with lightning-blast explosions on its sides. An aluminum warhead was mounted on top and contained a removable red plastic tailfin. The tailfin was hollow, making it a hidden compartment for tiny secret messages.
Removing the red base gave access to a “hidden atomic chamber”, a.k.a. a spinthariscope, in the warhead. Looking through the toy spinthariscope’s plastic lens while in a dark room revealed flashes of light. These scintillations were the by-product of an interaction of radioisotopes caused by polonium alpha particles striking the ring’s zinc sulfide screen.
While infusing minute traces of radioactive material into a kid’s toy wouldn’t fly today, advertisements for the ring assured that it was “perfectly safe” and contained “harmless” atomic elements. The minute traces of Polonium-210 in the spinthariscope had a half-life of about 140 days, meaning that any Atomic Bomb Rings still in existence today can no longer produce visible scintillations.

data.title: Holding Cellphone while driving is illegal, California court rules
data.author: firefoxd
data.article_summary: 加州上诉法院裁定，司机在驾驶时手持手机查看导航地图是违法的，即使只是查看而没有进行任何操作。这项裁定基于2016年通过的法律，旨在减少因现代手机发展导致的驾驶分心，鼓励司机将注意力集中在道路上。虽然车载支架固定的手机和单次滑动操作被豁免，但手持手机查看地图仍属违法。此裁定源于一名司机因手持手机查看地图而被罚款后上诉失败的案例。法院强调，法律禁止驾驶时“以任何目的”使用手机，包括查看地图等行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：法律语言的模糊性及其在司法解释中的影响

不同观点：
• ryandrake认为法律的语言过于模糊，立法者在撰写法律时使用了像“使用”（using）这样模糊的词语，导致需要法院和公众去猜测立法者的原意。他认为立法者本应在初次立法时更明确地表达意图，而不是依赖事后的司法解释或修正案。他批评这是立法者的懒政或不严谨，称之为“马虎的人写马虎的法律”。

• 法院在解释法律时，特别提到了立法过程中的记录，例如加州上诉法院指出，在法律起草时，立法委员会明确表示该法律将禁止“任何目的”的手机使用，并涵盖“所有分散注意力的移动设备相关行为”。这表明法院认为法律的原意是清晰的，即禁止所有可能导致驾驶分心的手机使用行为。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于法律语言的模糊性以及司法系统在解释这些模糊条款时的角色。ryandrake对立法者的不满集中在法律文本的不明确，而法院则试图通过立法记录来澄清法律的真实意图。
- 例子中提到的具体案件涉及一名司机因在驾驶时查看手机地图而被判有罪，但上诉法院将“使用”解释为仅限于手持手机进行通话和听讲，这显示了法律条文在实际应用中的复杂性和不确定性。

Mounted phones are exempted, according to the decision, but looking at a map while holding the phone would violate the current law, the court ruled.
(Allen G. Breed / Associated Press)
By
Salvador Hernandez

Think it’s all right to hold your cellphone while driving, as long as you’re just looking at a navigation app? Think again.
A state appeals court ruled Tuesday that the state law prohibiting  drivers from texting or talking on a cellphone while driving also makes it illegal to hold a  phone to look at a map on the screen.
The driver doesn’t need to be swiping or tapping at the navigation application to break the law, the court ruled. Just looking at the map on the screen, with the phone in hand, can justify getting pulled over to be ticketed.
Advertisement
When legislators adopted the current state law prohibiting drivers from “operating” a cellphone while driving, they did so “to reduce distracted driving resulting from advancements in modern phones and to encourage drivers to keep their eyes on the road,” the court of appeals ruled.
Mounted phones, and drivers operating them with a single swipe, are exempted, according to the decision, but looking at a map while holding the phone would violate the current law, the court ruled.
“Allowing a driver to hold a phone and view a mapping application, even if not touching the phone’s screen, would be contrary to the Legislature’s intent,”
according to the ruling
.
Advertisement
The court decision came after Nathaniel Gabriel Porter was ticketed after looking at a mapping application while holding his phone in his left hand and driving. Porter contested the ticket, but lost his initial court appearance and was ordered to pay the $158 fine, according to the court decision.
Porter appealed the decision with the appellate division of the Santa Clara County Superior Court and the decision was reversed, with the superior court at the time ruling that “operating” a cell phone required “active use or manipulation of the device.”
“Merely observing GPS directions on the phone does not constitute the kind of active use or manipulation to trigger an infraction,” the court ruled at the time.
Advertisement
But the California Court of Appeal for the sixth appellate district disagreed, and reversed the decision Tuesday, stating in its opinion that the law as written, and intended, says that looking at and holding  the phone while driving is a violation.
The current version of the law, adopted by the Legislature in 2016, was introduced after a previous court decision also raised questions about California’s version of the law regarding  phones and driving.
That case also arose when a driver was found guilty of violating the law because he was looking at a map on his  phone while driving. But when the case reached the court of appeal, it interpreted the word “using” in the law’s language as prohibiting listening and talking while holding a cellphone and driving.
That interpretation, according to the court’s written decision, was because the state law at the time stated phones had to be used in a way that allowed for “hands-free listening and talking.”
In 2016, the law was amended, with legislators pointing out that cellphones now acted more as “pocket-sized computers” and the law was too narrow.
In issuing its ruling on Tuesday, the California Court of Appeals noted that, when the current law was being drafted, the Assembly Committees on Transportation and Appropriations concluded that the new law would prohibit wireless phones from being used “for any purpose” while driving, and would include “all distracting mobile device-related behavior.”
Advertisement
That would include playing games on cellphones, browsing the internet, and under the recent ruling, looking at a map on the phone’s screen while holding the device.

data.title: The Prime Reasons to Avoid Amazon
data.author: DanAtC
data.article_summary:
这篇文章呼吁消费者在亚马逊“Prime Day”期间抵制购物，认为亚马逊在道德和伦理上存在严重问题。文章列举了亚马逊的四大问题：

1. **危害民权**：亚马逊曾向执法机构出售面部识别软件，该技术在识别少数族裔时准确率低，且亚马逊的Ring门铃让警方可以监视民众，包括和平抗议者。
2. **打击小企业**：亚马逊利用从其平台上小商家的数据来开发竞争产品，并通过低价竞争挤垮对手，实质上是垄断和企业间谍行为。
3. **侵犯劳工权利**：亚马逊对员工待遇差，工作条件恶劣，忽视人权。
4. **威胁民主**：亚马逊的垄断地位和对数据的控制使其对社会和政治体系构成威胁。

文章强调，只有消费者停止在亚马逊购物，才能真正遏制其不当行为，因为立法难以有效制约。

44475297.article_content:
The Prime Reasons to Avoid Amazon
July 5, 2025
Amazon’s now-legendary “Prime Day” is July 8-11. Much like Black Friday or Cyber Monday, this means sales on lots of items on Amazon’s vast marketplace, and as such many people flock to the giant’s website to get sweet deals on everything from computers to small kitchen appliances and more. While many of us are feeling the financial crunch more than ever, I urge you, dear reader, to resist the allure. I don’t typically have strong opinions about where people chose to shop or how they decide to spend their heard-earned money, but in this post I hope to lay out a convincing case for why Amazon is full-stop evil, no caveats, and is undeserving of your money on a moral and ethical level no matter what your values are. Amazon needs to be stopped, and legislation will not do so. Only its loyal consumers – who keep the beast alive – can do that by taking their money elsewhere. No matter your political or personal beliefs, I'm certain Amazon violates them in one way or another, and you should vote with your dollar by buying from other places whenever possible. Here’s why.
Table of Contents
Amazon is an Enemy of Civil Rights
Amazon Is An Enemy of Small Businesses
Amazon Is An Enemy of Human Rights and Workers
Amazon Is An Enemy of Democracy
This Problem Does Not Exist in a Vacuum
Facing Reality and Taking Next Steps
Amazon Is An Enemy of Civil Rights
Do you believe that black lives matter? Do you think police have too much funding, too little oversight, are a tool of an oppressive regime, and/or are a private police force for the rich to keep the poor and minorities in line? Well guess what:
up until 2020
Amazon proudly sold their facial recognition software (called “Rekognition”) to law enforcement agencies all cross the country. Like every other facial recognition software out there, this system was notoriously
bad at accurately identifying minorities
, mainly people of color and women (if you have Netflix, there's a whole movie about this called
Coded Bias
, which I highly recommend). Amazon only stopped for PR reasons at the start of the George Floyd protests, and even then they only issued a “one-year moratorium.” This has since been
extended indefinitely
, but frankly that doesn’t matter. It’s still just PR. Why do I say that? Because for one, that ban only applies to the US. Amazon is still free to sell their faulty facial recognition services to other countries and industries. Second, Amazon still gives police across the nation unfettered access to
Ring doorbells
, allowing police to have vast real-time surveillance networks paid for by private citizens who may not even know law enforcement has this sort of access. Amazon is actively helping police spy on and identify – poorly – everyone, even
peaceful protesters
.
Amazon Is An Enemy of Small Businesses
“Well I think all lives matter,” you may say to yourself, “and I support our law enforcement officers.” That’s cool. If you’re more right-leaning, you probably believe in the free market and you’ll likely be furious to know that
Amazon actively crushes small businesses
. To be clear, I'm not talking about the free market where they simply provide a better product/service and win over customers from the other guys. Amazon has been repeatedly proven to use data gathered from small merchants who use their marketplace to create competing products, avoiding the financial hit of the mistakes that those smaller businesses may have already made in marketing, pricing, or production. (I believe this is the exact sort of data that would be covered by nearly every standard non-disclosure agreement that nearly every company uses these days, by the way.) Not that it matters, because Amazon can also just use their massive empire to
undercut the competition
, selling products at a massive loss until the competitor is eventually driven out of business, then bouncing prices back up to profit-making levels once there’s no alternatives to compete with. The use of this data in the first place isn’t just free market sorting itself out, it’s straight up corporate espionage. Amazon leverages their highly-invasive platform (which is so ubiquitous that to NOT sell on Amazon is practically a death sentence, thus forcing sellers and small business owners to submit to their monopoly or face extinction, and thereby dismantling the classic disingenuous “just go somewhere else” argument) to harvest sensitive business data and then use their resources to take the hit until the smaller guys can’t anymore and fold. In any other scenario, this would be corporate spying and illegal monopolizing. Even if it wasn’t illegal, I’d have a hard time believing any free-market enthusiast actually has no problem with this.
Amazon Is An Enemy of Human Rights and Workers

no such thing

data.title: macOS Icon History
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 本文简要回顾了macOS系统图标的历史演变，并重点介绍了macOS 26引入的重大设计变革——“Liquid Glass”新外观。此次更新中，图标从实体风格转向更柔和、闪亮的玻璃效果，图标形状变得更加圆润，且元素不再超出图标矩形范围。作者BasicAppleGuy记录了系统图标多年来的变化，并在2025年6月陆续在社交媒体上发布了多款应用图标的更新，包括系统设置、文件夹、便签、笔记、信息、计算器、游戏中心、地图、播客和Photo Booth等。此次视觉革新是macOS设计史上最显著的一次。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果图标设计演变的评价与对比

不同观点：

• rezmason：对新图标设计持正面态度，并推荐了自己的Mac屏保程序"Iconic"，该程序展示了Mac历史上值得注意的图标。

• user3939382：怀念macOS 9和BeOS的UI设计，认为现代macOS设计无法带来同样的愉悦感，考虑回归旧系统但担心浏览器等兼容性问题。

macOS Icon History
2025
macOS
Icon
Apple History
Jun 23
Written By
BasicAppleGuy
Documenting the evolution of macOS system icons over the past several decades.
With macOS 26, Apple has announced a dramatically new look to their UI: Liquid Glass. Solid material icon elements give way to softer, shinier, glassier icons. The rounded rectangle became slightly more rounded, and Apple eliminated the ability for icon elements to extend beyond the icon rectangle (as seen in the current icons for GarageBand, Photo Booth, Dictionary, etc.).
With this release being one of the most dramatic visual overhauls of macOS's design, I wanted to begin a collection chronicling the evolution of the system icons over the years. I've been rolling these out on social media over the past week and will continue to add to and update this collection slowly over the summer. Enjoy!

data.title: Haskell, Reverse Polish Notation, and Parsing
data.author: mw_1
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在学习Haskell语言、处理逆波兰表示法（Reverse Polish Notation, RPN）以及解析理论过程中的一段经历。作者最初为了找工作开始探索函数式编程，并在朋友的建议下选择了Haskell。在构建一个RPN计算器的过程中，作者经历了从命令式编程向函数式编程的思维转变。Haskell强调函数的数学抽象，数据不可变，且通过递归和表达式解决问题，而非使用循环和可变状态。作者通过自然数的递归定义、λ函数和柯里化等概念逐步深入理解Haskell，并体会到函数式编程的简洁与强大。最终，作者成功实现了一个RPN计算器，并从中获得了对Haskell更深层次的理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对逆波兰表示法（RPN）和递归编程的看法，以及函数式编程与传统编程（如C语言）的对比。

不同观点：
• [jcalvinowens] 认为RPN是一种通过重新定义问题语义来简化问题的强大工具。他个人在函数式编程中的困难在于难以实现迭代，常常因为设计失误而需要重写代码，而在C语言中，即使架构设计失误，他通常也能重用部分代码。他将此归因于可能只是经验不足。

• [kibwen] 赞同RPN和栈机器的优美和被低估，但对递归持保留意见。他认为递归让程序的执行时间变得不可控，并且递归不如循环直观和高效。他更倾向于使用显式的循环结构，而不是担心任何随机的函数调用是否会递归。除非语言保证尾递归并有明确的语法支持，否则他更愿意使用不支持递归的语言。

• [jacksonslipock] 表示通过讨论对单子（monad）有了初步理解，但预计几天后会忘记，计划再次阅读。

补充讨论：
- [jcalvinowens] 的观点中提到了函数式编程中的迭代困难，可能与不熟悉或经验不足有关。
- [kibwen] 对递归的效率提出了质疑，特别是对运行时处理无限栈帧的担忧，强调了显式循环的可控性和效率。
- [jacksonslipock] 的评论虽然简短，但反映了函数式编程概念（如单子）的学习曲线和理解难度。

争议焦点：
- 递归与循环的优劣：[jcalvinowens] 认为递归编程有其挑战性，而[kibwen] 则明确表示递归不如循环，特别是在执行时间和效率方面。

My Side Quest into Haskell, Reverse Polish Notation, and Parsing
26 Jun, 2025
My Journey into Haskell: Building a Reverse Polish Notation Calculator
Introduction: A Side Quest
In my attempt to get my first paycheck, aka get a job, I have led myself down a fascinating rabbit hole into functional programming, mathematical notation, and parsing theory. This is the story of how I discovered Haskell, tackled reverse Polish notation, and learned about monadic parsing along the way.
My journey began when my friend Jackson Slipock encouraged me to explore functional programming. After a quick Google search, I landed on Haskell as my first functional language. Around the same time, during a networking call about job opportunities, someone mentioned reverse Polish notation. The idea struck me: why not build a reverse Polish notation calculator in Haskell?
What could have been a simple weekend project became weeks of deep learning. This blog chronicles that journey, drawing heavily from Graham Hutton's excellent book Programming in Haskell, which I highly recommend. What you're reading is my attempt to learn something deeply, implement it myself, and then teach it to others.
From Imperative to Functional: A Mental Shift
Coming from a background in Python and C—languages I'm comfortable with after a couple years of experience—Haskell represented a fundamental shift in thinking. Both Python and C are imperative languages that share similar concepts: loops, mutable data, global state, and variables that can be modified. The transition between them never required a major mental adjustment.
Functional programming throws all of that out the window.
In Haskell, functions are mathematical abstractions. Given the same input, a function will always produce the same output. There are no global variables, and data is immutable once created. Instead of writing a series of statements that accomplish a task, functional programming encourages building expressions that naturally compose together.
This is why Haskell has no loops. Instead, it pushes you to think recursively, building solutions through expressions that elegantly combine to produce results.
Why Choose Functional Programming?
The benefits became clear as I progressed: functional code tends to be more concise, easier to understand, and less prone to bugs. Haskell excels at representing complex ideas in just a few lines of code, and it makes translating mathematical concepts into working programs remarkably straightforward. As someone who majored in math and genuinely enjoys it, this felt incredibly satisfying.
These concepts might seem abstract at first—I certainly struggled with them initially. But they become clearer with practice, and keeping them in mind helps when encountering Haskell code for the first time. My first real "aha!" moment came when implementing merge sort, but before we get there, let's explore some things that were new to me as a first time functional programmer.
Recursive Types: Building Natural Numbers from Scratch
Let me start with a classic example that illustrates Haskell's elegance. Here's how you can define natural numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, 4...) recursively:

data.title: Is It Cake? How Our Brain Deciphers Materials
data.author: dnetesn
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了现代社交媒体和娱乐中流行的“这是蛋糕吗？”现象，即通过视觉欺骗让人误以为某些物体是蛋糕。这种视觉错觉与历史上艺术作品通过材质欺骗视觉的手法相似，比如米开朗基罗的大理石雕塑《大卫》和Giovanni Strazza的《戴面纱的圣母》。这种现象引发了对人类识别物体材质能力的关注，尽管这一能力对生存至关重要，但直到最近才成为神经科学的研究重点。

文章还提到，自2001年Edward H. Adelson的论文《看见材质》发表以来，材质感知研究迅速发展。最近发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的一项研究提出了一种广泛的方法，通过行为数据识别出人类大脑在理解材质时考虑的36个基本维度。这种研究不仅揭示了我们如何识别材质，还为了解大脑如何高效处理信息提供了新视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类能够通过视觉预测物品的口感或触感

不同观点：
• [WJW]认为人类拥有一种特殊能力，即通过观察周围任意物品，能够准确预测其放入嘴中的味道或感觉。这种能力可能源自婴儿时期习惯将各种物品放入口中的行为，并惊奇地发现这种能力在成年后依然有效。
  
• [webdevver]对[WJW]的观点进行了幽默的延伸，提出未来科技如Tesla Bot可能会出错，比如误将湿海绵当作食物端给人类，质疑这种预测能力在面对高度智能化或自动化场景时的可靠性。

补充讨论：
• [WJW]的评论中隐含了对人类早期发展行为（如婴儿通过口腔探索世界）的长远影响的思考，强调了这种行为对成年后某些直觉性能力的潜在影响。
  
• [webdevver]的评论引入科技进步可能对人类直觉和感知能力带来的挑战，暗示未来技术误操作可能导致人类依赖的直觉能力失效。

争议焦点：人类通过视觉预测物品口感的能力在未来科技背景下是否依然可靠。

Explore
O
ne of the greatest questions of the modern age is: Is it cake? As in: Is it an
espresso machine
, or cake?
Paint can
, or cake?
Air fryer
, or …? Millions of viewers have watched rapt as TikTok  bakers slice or bite into inedible-looking objects with fluffy, frosting-filled innards … or have tuned into
Is It Cake?
, the aptly named Netflix show. Why? As a form of entertainment, this kind of visual trick is hardly new. For centuries, artists have delighted in fooling us into thinking one material is another. From Michelangelo’s marble
David,
with his sinewy, soft-looking flesh, to Giovanni Strazza’s
Veiled Virgin
, draped in a marble veil that appears gossamer thin. What makes these illusions so mesmerizing? Maybe it’s because these classic works of art and these modern social media ruses test our ability to use an underappreciated skill that’s been essential to our species’ survival: identifying what stuff is made of.

Over the past century, neuroscience has made great strides in understanding how the brain visually identifies objects—like mugs, trees, and faces. But the question of how we recognize what those objects are made of (smooth porcelain, rough bark, soft flesh) has been overlooked until relatively recently. “Our world contains both things and stuff, but things tend to get the attention,” wrote Edward H. Adelson, an MIT neuroscientist whose provocative 2001
paper
, “On Seeing Stuff: The Perception of Materials by Humans and Machines,” spurred a flurry of material perception research.
1
“Yet materials are just as important as objects are,” he wrote. “Our world involves steel and glass, paper and plastic, food and drink, leather and lace, ice and snow, not to mention blood sweat and tears.”
I
t’s strange that the field of material perception is so new, considering how essential the ability to decipher what things are made of is. “When we look around our world, everything is made of materials,” says Alexandra Schmid, a postdoc at the National Institutes of Health’s National Institute of Mental Health. “And we need that information to know how to interact with that world.” Recognizing what an object is made of tells us—as it told our ancestors—how we can interact with it: Can we squeeze it? Eat it? Touch it without getting burned or scratched? Pick it up? (And if so, using how much force?) Material perception helps us spot the glimmer of potentially potable water, and sort firm, fresh-looking fruit from wrinkled, rotten ones. Humans, like chimpanzees, use material properties like hardness to determine if a rock is a suitable weapon or tool. And brains that are optimally tuned to making these sorts of decisions efficiently and accurately are essential to survival and reproductive success, especially as our evolutionary predecessors navigated the travails of early human history.

Even when we’re not seeing a material, our minds can fill in the blank of what it should look like.
Since Adelson’s provocative paper two decades ago, the study of material perception has exploded. Recent studies have investigated how we categorize specific materials, such as wood or metal, as well as isolated material properties, including hardness, color, or elasticity. Dozens of papers exclusively tackle our perception of “gloss.” Yet despite the neuroscientific progress studying how our brains make sense of this narrow band of materials and properties, until recently, researchers didn’t have the foggiest sense of the span or range of materials humans perceive.
Now, a
paper
recently published in the
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
proposes a sweeping, generalized approach to understanding material perception.
2
Most prior research has focused on testing specific material qualities that scientists predetermined to be important to perception—such as shininess, hardness, or color. Schmidt and her coauthors of the
PNAS
paper took a different approach: letting patterns emerge naturally from behavioral data. Using methods borrowed from machine learning, they were able to uncover 36 fundamental dimensions that our brains consider to understand materials.

文章还提到，自2001年Edward H. Adelson的论文《看见材质》发表以来，材质感知研究迅速发展。最近发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的一项研究提出了一种广泛的方法，通过行为数据识别出人类大脑在理解材质时考虑的36个基本维度。这种研究不仅揭示了我们如何识别材质，还为了解大脑如何高效处理信息提供了新视角。

data.title: Pet ownership and cognitive functioning in later adulthood across pet types
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了宠物饲养与晚年认知功能之间的关系，特别是不同类型的宠物（如狗、猫、鸟、鱼）以及不同年龄组对认知衰退的影响。通过分析欧洲健康与退休调查的数据，研究发现饲养宠物与认知功能（执行功能和情景记忆）的衰退减缓相关。具体来说，狗和猫的饲养与较慢的认知衰退有关，而鸟和鱼则没有这种关联。年龄组并未显著影响这种关系。研究表明，饲养狗和猫可能有助于减缓认知衰退，支持健康的认知老化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：养宠物（特别是狗）对心理健康和认知功能的潜在影响

不同观点：
• [thenaturalist] 认为养狗对心理健康和情绪调节有显著积极影响，尤其是对有ADHD的人。他提到养狗让他变得更加冷静、减少压力，并且通过观察狗反复尝试而不纠结于过去的错误，帮助他改善了自我信任和执行功能。此外，养狗还增加了他与陌生人之间的积极互动。

• [montroser] 质疑这种因果关系的确定性，认为可能只是选择养狗的人本身就更有可能保持认知功能的健康，而不是养狗导致了这种结果。他承认养狗可能带来健康益处，但认为需要更多证据来证明因果关系。

• [ludicrousdispla] 批评了科学出版物中的图表标注问题，指出某个图表没有清楚标明时间单位的定义，也没有解释“时间0”代表什么，这可能导致读者误解数据。

• [bestouff] 引用了研究结果，指出狗和猫的饲养与较慢的认知衰退有关联，而养鸟和养鱼则没有这种关联。

• [torbid] 质疑为什么养鸟没有像养猫一样有类似的效果，并提出是否因为养哺乳动物（如狗或猫）更重要，或者是否存在隐藏变量（如租房时养小型动物更容易获得许可）影响了研究结果。

• [luqtas] 希望看到控制更多变量（如爱好和社会活动参与）的研究，认为仅仅看是否与他人同住并不能充分解释养宠物对认知功能的潜在好处，并提到一些与社会隔离但无朋友的已婚人士可能会在被动娱乐中度过大量时间。

- 对研究设计和数据解释的批评，特别是关于变量控制和科学出版物中图表描述的准确性。
- 讨论了不同类型宠物（如狗、猫、鸟、鱼）对心理健康和认知功能的潜在不同影响。
- 提出了隐藏变量（如租房规定、社会活动参与度）可能对研究结果产生影响的可能性。

44474894.article_content:
Longitudinal relationships between pet ownership and cognitive functioning in later adulthood across pet types and individuals’ ages
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Human behaviour
Psychology
Abstract
Pet ownership has been shown to have a positive influence on cognitive functioning and cognitive decline in late adulthood. However, there is limited understanding of how different species of pets are associated with these outcomes in different age groups. This study employed a multilevel modelling approach using data from eight waves of the Survey of Health and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) to longitudinally examine: (1) the relationship between pet ownership and cognitive decline over 18 years among adults aged 50 and older, (2) The moderating role of younger vs. older age subgroups on this relationship, and (3) the distinct role of owning dogs, cats, birds, and fish. The targeted cognitive domains were executive functioning and episodic memory. Results confirmed that pet ownership is associated with slower decline in both cognitive domains. While age group did not moderate this relationship, differences emerged in the relationship between cognitive decline and individual pet species. Dog and cat ownership was associated with slower cognitive decline compared to no pet ownership; bird and fish ownership showed no such association. These findings suggest that dog and cat ownership might act as a protective factor aiding to slow down cognitive decline, thus contributing to healthy cognitive ageing.

. Therefore, it is important to investigate potential avenues to support cognitive health across the lifespan.
With regards to individual lifestyle factors, previous research has shown that, for example, an adherence to a Mediterranean- or DASH-style diet rich in vegetables, fruits, whole grains and unsaturated fats; sleeping 7–8 h per night with limited night-time fragmentation; regular participation in social clubs or volunteering; enrolment in adult-education courses; or employment in cognitively demanding occupations, are related to reduced or delayed deterioration of cognitive functioning

data.title: How to not pay your taxes legally, apparently
data.author: jimhi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了企业主如何利用多种合法手段减少或避免缴税，包括成立有限责任公司（LLC）或C类公司来抵扣各种费用。文中提到彼得·蒂尔通过罗斯个人退休账户（Roth IRA）避税的例子，并讨论了 Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS) 税 exemption，允许企业在出售前等待5年以避免前1000万美元的税款。此外，文中还介绍了通过设立信托为亲属避税的方法，以及利用波多黎各的税收优惠政策。文章强调这些策略在某些州可能不适用，并提到大学也会鼓励利用这些避税手段。总的来说，这些方法虽然合法，但存在道德和法律的灰色地带。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过合法手段避税的道德性、合法性和操作性

不同观点：
• SoftTalker：认为只要法律允许，避税是合理的。如果政府想要收税，应该简化税法，避免漏洞。人们发现并利用合法避税手段是正常行为。

• lucianbr：质疑提前多年准备避税策略的可行性。如果公司没有达到预期价值或者超出预期价值，该如何处理？

• burnt-resistor：指出美国富人拥有多种合法避税手段，但放弃国籍的成本高昂，且面临诸多限制。美国和厄立特里亚是唯一两个对海外公民征税的国家。

• trollbridge：认为文章标题有误导性。如果公司盈利，很难合法避税。如果公司亏损，可能找到愿意收购亏损公司的买家。

• daft_pink：指出创建一个价值超过1000万美元的公司并不简单，特别是在硅谷之外。QSBS（合格小企业股票）的税收优惠在实际操作中可能导致双重征税。

• HWR_14：对Thiel如何利用Roth IRA购买PayPal股份表示困惑，因为通常不能用Roth IRA投资自己工作的公司。

• eli：认为识别未来价值巨大的股票是避税策略中的难点。

• sailfast：认为问题不在于个人不缴税，而在于富人通过游说改变税法，创造隐蔽的免税条款。

• v5v3：引用Dave Chapelle的观点，指出由于政治捐款者的利益，政治家不会主动关闭这些税收漏洞。

• giarc：建议更新文章，提供更多相关信息和参考链接。

• bgnn：建议创业者移居没有资本利得税的国家，如荷兰。

44474531.article_content:
Business owners have the most flexibility of everyone to not pay their taxes. I personally think these things are questionable but its what I have seen others do over the last few years and what has been recommended to me by every top accounting firm in New York.
It is incredibly simple to spin up an LLC or C corp and expense all kinds of things. Employees don’t get this benefit.
Peter Thiel famously bought his Paypal shares (which were valued at a few cents when he founded the company) into his Roth IRA account. When he will turn 65* (thanks niklasbabel* he is not 65 yet!), he able to access the billions that the Paypal equity was worth with 0 tax on it.
But what if you want the money sooner? Are there other methods?
Of course there is. The first one is QSBS Tax which many startup founders still don’t seem to know about.
This is the Qualified Small Business Stock Tax Exclusion. Basically as long as you wait 5 years before selling the business, you won’t be taxed on the first $10 million dollars. This isn’t some loophole, this is exactly what it was intended for so that people are encouraged to take risks.
Let’s say your company is hot and you can sell it within 2 years though. Is there a loophole?
Of course there is.
When you get acquired you simply sell yourself extended options which you don’t activate until the 5 years have passed.
Let’s say you are going to make more than $10 million dollars though. Let’s say you sell for $100 million. How do you avoid that pesky tax on the other 90?
It’s called Trust Stacking. QSBS let’s you exclude up to $10 million in taxes “per person.”
So you simply create a trust for everyone else you know and fill it with what you think will become about $10 million worth when you exit.
If you have a wife and kids for a long time you can just make one for each. Super easy.
If you are single, you can create one for future relatives and kids with a placeholder beneficiary. That would likely be someone like your current or future spouse.
If you end up never having kids, you can spend it on the placeholder.
Let’s say that covers only $40 million in tax avoidance, who else can you ping?
This is where it gets into much murkier waters.
You ask your parents to create a Trust for you. A “trust for me?” you ask? But you are the one with the money, not them! They put in say $1000 dollars and use that to acquire just enough of your shares that you think will add up to another $10 million. Now you’re up to $50 million easy.
Now it’s free reign. You look at your siblings, your cousins, anyone you can trust.
Now every trust you make needs a Trustee. They can’t be related or married to you. Ideally its just a business partner of yours who you trust to do whatever you want.
The following states will have tax complications with these methods:
Arizona
California
Colorado
Indiana
Kansas
Utah
Lousiana
Missisippi
New Mexico
Oregon
South Carolina
What if you run out distant relatives and future children? You still have more money you want to avoid tax on!
Well you likely can’t completely avoid it, but you can reduce it.
It’s too late to give up your USA citizenship. Instead, the same year you plan on selling your stock, buy a house and move to Puerto Rico. Long-term capital gains are reduced only in that area for the USA. Don’t worry you can just move out of Puerto Rico a year or so later.
By the way these various loopholes are encouraged by Universities. If you want even more potential loopholes, talk to your University Alumni Association about how “flexible” their donation system is. The earlier in the exit process for your company, the better. They have a myriad of ways to help you reduce taxes in exchange for a some % of the money getting donated to them.

• SoftTalker：认为只要法律允许，避税是合理的。如果政府想要收税，应该简化税法，避免漏洞。人们发现并利用合法避税手段是正常行为。

• lucianbr：质疑提前多年准备避税策略的可行性。如果公司没有达到预期价值或者超出预期价值，该如何处理？

• burnt-resistor：指出美国富人拥有多种合法避税手段，但放弃国籍的成本高昂，且面临诸多限制。美国和厄立特里亚是唯一两个对海外公民征税的国家。

• trollbridge：认为文章标题有误导性。如果公司盈利，很难合法避税。如果公司亏损，可能找到愿意收购亏损公司的买家。

• daft_pink：指出创建一个价值超过1000万美元的公司并不简单，特别是在硅谷之外。QSBS（合格小企业股票）的税收优惠在实际操作中可能导致双重征税。

• HWR_14：对Thiel如何利用Roth IRA购买PayPal股份表示困惑，因为通常不能用Roth IRA投资自己工作的公司。

• eli：认为识别未来价值巨大的股票是避税策略中的难点。

• sailfast：认为问题不在于个人不缴税，而在于富人通过游说改变税法，创造隐蔽的免税条款。

• v5v3：引用Dave Chapelle的观点，指出由于政治捐款者的利益，政治家不会主动关闭这些税收漏洞。

• giarc：建议更新文章，提供更多相关信息和参考链接。

• bgnn：建议创业者移居没有资本利得税的国家，如荷兰。

• gist：详细解释QSBS的适用条件和限制，指出并不是所有情况下都适用。买家通常决定是否收购公司资产而不是股份，以避免未来责任。

• niklasbabel：质疑文章中关于Peter Thiel年龄的描述，指出文章中的时间线不准确。

• edoceo：认为文章标题有误导性，文章讨论的是如何避免税务事件，而不是不缴应缴税款。这是一种改变资金税务类别的已知方法。

• anonymousiam：分享与IRS打交道的负面经历，认为IRS不诚实，且富人可以通过聘请好的税务律师与IRS斗争并获胜。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到QSBS的适用条件和实际操作中的复杂性，以及不同国家税收政策的差异。
• 对Peter Thiel的案例有多种解读和疑问，特别是关于Roth IRA的操作。
• 对IRS的批评集中在效率低下和不公平对待纳税人，特别是对于没有资源聘请律师的普通纳税人。

争议焦点：
• 合法避税的道德性：一些人认为只要法律允许，避税是合理的；另一些人则认为富人通过游说改变税法，创造不公平的优势。
• QSBS的实际操作和适用性：不同评论者对QSBS的实际效果和适用条件有不同看法。

data.title: The Calculator-on-a-Chip (2015)
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了20世纪60年代末到70年代初，计算器行业致力于将所有计算器功能集成到一个芯片上，即"单芯片计算器"的开发历程。早期计算器如1968年的Canon Canola 130S需要13块电路板，而1970年的Sharp QT-8B则使用了Rockwell的4片芯片组。最终，多家公司成功推出了单芯片计算器，包括Mostek的MK6010和Texas Instruments的TMS1802NC。其中，Mostek的MK6010于1970年11月问世，首次应用于Busicom Junior计算器，取代了原机型中的两块电路板和22个中规模集成电路。虽然该芯片集成了计算器逻辑，但仍需额外元件驱动显示器。Mostek在极短时间内完成了这一突破性设计，推动了消费级计算器的普及。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Commodore与德州仪器（TI）之间的竞争及技术策略，以及对经典计算器技术的讨论

不同观点：
• **[classichasclass的观点]**：Commodore的创始人Jack Tramiel通过收购MOS Technology实现了垂直整合，从而能够自行生产芯片。这帮助Commodore在与德州仪器的竞争中获得优势，尤其是在德州仪器使用相同芯片生产价格更低的计算器导致Commodore被削价竞争的情况下。最终，Commodore成功将德州仪器挤出家用电脑市场，完成了某种意义上的“复仇”。

• **[Dwedit的观点]**：Dwedit更关注技术创新的角度，提到Sinclair Scientific Calculator在技术上的突破。这款计算器使用了为普通四功能计算器设计的低功耗芯片，但依然实现了科学计算器的功能，展示了在有限硬件条件下进行技术创新的可能性。

补充讨论：
• **技术整合与竞争策略**：classichasclass强调了通过收购和整合技术供应链来获得竞争优势的商业策略，尤其是在早期计算机和计算器市场中的应用。Jack Tramiel通过这种策略成功反制德州仪器。

• **技术创新与限制突破**：Dwedit提出的Sinclair Scientific Calculator的例子展示了如何在硬件限制下进行创新，强调了技术突破在产品设计中的重要性。

争议焦点：虽然没有直接的争议，但两者讨论的角度不同，一个侧重商业竞争和策略，另一个侧重技术创新和工程挑战。两者都反映了早期计算器和计算机行业发展的不同方面。

44473871.article_content:
Calculator Articles
Home
>
Collecting Calculators
The Arrival of the "Calculator-on-a-Chip"
During the late 1960s and early 1970s a major aim of the calculator electronics companies was to integrate all of the functionality of a calculator into one integrated circuit, so producing a
"Calculator-on-a Chip".
© 2015 Nigel Tout
This is a new article which was not originally in "The International Calculator Collector".
Introduction
As told in the section
"
The Story of the Race to Develop the Pocket Electronic Calculator
"
, from the mid-1960s one of the aims of the
electronics industry was to integrate more of the functionality of a calculator into fewer integrated circuits so that less components were required and calculators became smaller and cheaper.
Inside the
Canon
Canola 130S
.  This is a typical calculator of about 1968 and requires 13 circuit boards full of components.
The degree of integration was gradually improved.  Here the
Sharp
QT-8B
of 1970 has a 4-piece chipset manufactured by Rockwell.
The development effort eventually led to several companies introducing, around the same time, integrated circuits that provided all of the functionality of a calculator in one integrated circuit - that is they employed a, so-called,
"Calculator-on-a-chip".
Note that the early "Calculator-on-a-chip" examples still required additional components for driving displays.
The first "Calculator-on-a-chip" integrated circuits produced were:
Mostek
MK6010 (MK5010
)
Texas Instruments
TMS1802NC
(
TMS0102
)
GI
G250
Mostek
MK6010
(
MK5010
)
The article
"The Calculator that spawned the Microprocessor: The Busicom 141-PF calculator and the Intel 4004 microprocessor"
explained that while the Japanese calculator company Busicom was developing with Intel the electronics for its 141-PF calculator, which was to lead to the Intel 4004 microprocessor, this very innovative Japanese calculator manufacturer had also commissioned Mostek of Dallas to push the limits of integration of calculator electronics by putting all the functionality on a single chip.
Mostek was a new start-up company and desperate for sales.  It estimated that it could design the layout for a single calculator chip in six weeks, but the first circuit design failed preliminary testing and the design
eventually took three months.  After frenzied development work the first ever "Calculator-on-a-chip" was produced in November 1970, as told in
"The Chip"
on an archive of the Mostek site
[1]
.
The chip was given the designation Mostek
MK6010
and was immediately put to use in the
Busicom
Junior
small desktop calculator, as shown below.
The cover of a Busicom
Junior
calculator has been removed to reveal the circuit board showing the single Mostek LSI chip mounted on a plug-in chip carrier.
Cutting edge technology of 1971, the Mostek
MK6010
"calculator on a chip" in a Busicom
Junior
calculator.  The integrated circuit illustrated is date coded 7125 (i.e. 1971, week 25) and is also marked with the 'NCM' logo (
N
ippon
C
alculating
M
achines—the original name of Busicom Corp.).
The IC is mounted on a small piece of circuit board which plugs sideways into the black socket.
"Calculator on a Chip"
The magazine "Electronics" for Feb 1st. 1971 proclaimed
[2]
:
"The apparent winner in the race to produce a calculator on a chip has hit the wire.  Mostek Corp., of Carrolton, Texas, is now producing such a chip for Japan's Busicom Corp. ...  The
180-mil-square [0.18 inches-square (4.6 mm-square)] chip contains the logic for a four function 12-digit calculator - more than 2,100 transistors in 360 gates plus 160 flip-flops.  Its promise of lower labor costs means a
giant step toward a calculator for the consumer market. ... ... Busicom's initial use of the chip will be as a direct replacement in its Junior model calculator now being distributed in the U.S. by National Cash Register."
The chip held in the hand replaces the two circuit boards full of components, including 22 MSI (Medium Scale Integration) integrated circuits in the
original
Busicom
Junior
desktop calculator to produce the
new version Busicom
Junior
.
The single chip, using a p-channel semiconductor process, replaced 22 chips in the
original Busicom
Junior
desktop calculator and reduced the number of circuit boards from two to one in the
new version Busicom
Junior
.  Note that separate transistors were still needed as high-voltage display drivers.
The article continues ... "
Busicom asked if Mostek could put a whole calculator on a chip. Cash [Berry Cash, Mostek's marketing vice president] says he balked at that but felt sure Mostek could put the logic on two or three chips
even though the company had no previous experience in calculators. ...  It decided to try for one chip, and consequently allotted six weeks for its layout.  It took three months—and made meeting the rest of the
schedule very difficult.
"
Mostek of Dallas was then less than 2 years old and desperately needed the income that this project would generate.

data.title: Why I left my tech job to work on chronic pain
data.author: glasscannon
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：慢性疼痛的成因、处理方法及其与心理因素的关系

不同观点：
• **aspbee555** 认为，慢性疼痛和工作压力、不健康的工作环境密切相关，通过离开高压工作环境并调整生活方式，可以显著改善疼痛和整体健康状况。他强调了工作环境对身心健康的影响。

• **algo_lover** 对相关文章和讨论的不透明性表示不满，认为文章没有直接提到“疼痛再处理理论”（Pain Reprocessing Theory），并质疑为什么不能直接给出解决方案，而是让读者感觉在被推销某种东西。

• **glasscannon** 分享了自己应对慢性疼痛的经历，并计划通过博客系列探讨这个话题，呼吁对此有热情的人一起讨论。

• **kianN** 强调了慢性疼痛与回避行为的关系，主张在活动量上找到一个中间地带，以避免过度避免运动导致疼痛加剧。他指出，简单的疗法和日常运动可以有效缓解慢性疼痛。

• **foobiekr** 通过个人经历发现，慢性疼痛与心理压力有显著关联，并提供了相关研究链接。他提醒大家注意心理因素对疼痛的影响。

• **mattgreenrocks** 描述了自己因慢性反流而经历的痛苦，认为其症状与心理因素有关，并正在通过改变生活方式（如换工作）来尝试解决。

• **nwienert** 警告不要将所有慢性疼痛都归因于心理问题，强调有些疼痛是由真实的物理健康问题引起的，不要被误导或放弃寻找诊断。

• **NoTranslationL** 介绍了一款用于跟踪慢性疼痛并帮助找到根本原因的应用程序，愿意回答相关问题并祝愿其他患者早日康复。

• **ThinkBeat** 对通过新闻通讯等方式 monetize 康复过程表示怀疑，认为这些解决方案缺乏医学研究支持，并警告大家不要轻信这些“万灵药”。

• **Aurornis** 指出，某些人将特定技术视为所有慢性疼痛的通用解决方案，并警告不要将这些方法过度推广，强调需要根据具体情况选择合适的治疗方法。

• **littlexsparkee** 分享了自己应对身体疼痛的经历和方法，推荐了一些康复书籍和补充剂，并强调了心理和身体恢复的难度。

• **quicktemp42** 描述了自己在牙科手术后经历的慢性头痛，尽管医学检查显示正常，但疼痛仍然存在，寻求其他患者的建议。

• **anon1685212382** 通过个人经验分享了应对慢性健康问题的工程方法，强调了压力管理和正确使用身体的重要性，并警告不要轻信网络上的健身视频。

补充讨论：
• **bentt** 提到了Dr. John Sarno的工作，询问其与讨论话题的关系，可能涉及到心理因素对疼痛的影响。

• **doddpronter** 通过朋友的例子说明了身体健康与心理幸福感之间的密切关系，强调了减少压力和热爱工作的重要性。

争议焦点：慢性疼痛是否主要由心理因素引起，以及某些解决方案是否适用于所有患者。例如，kianN和Aurornis都指出，不能将特定疗法过度推广为所有慢性疼痛的通用解决方案。

主要讨论点：金融行业中的道德问题以及个人在追求财富过程中的迷失

不同观点：
• jmogly 认为金融行业，特别是抵押贷款和信用评估领域，存在严重的 dehumanizing（非人性化）现象。他描述了自己在抵押公司工作的经历，强调了在工作中将人简化为数据和事实的过程。他还分享了一次面试经历，认为那家从事 "factoring" 的公司尽管表面上看起来符合道德，但实际上却像高利贷，充满了对物质财富的追求，并使从业者远离了“自然善良”。

• jmogly 进一步反思，认为这些金融从业者由于对个人物质财富的无尽追求，逐渐失去了对世界美好事物的价值认知，走上了偏离道德的道路。他质疑是什么或谁导致了他们这样的迷失。

• gruez 没有直接表达自己的观点，而是通过分享一篇来自彭博社的文章链接，提供了一个更为批判的金融行业评论。这篇文章可能从私募股权 veterans（老兵）的角度对金融行业进行批评，为 jmogly 的观点提供了一定支持或补充。

• mitchbob 同样没有直接发表意见，而是通过分享一篇纽约时报的文章链接，为讨论提供了更多背景资料。该文章可能进一步探讨了金融行业中的道德问题，与 jmogly 的经历和反思形成呼应。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于金融行业是否本质上存在 dehumanizing 和道德问题。jmogly 以个人经历为例，描述了该行业的非人性化操作及其对从业者价值观的负面影响。
• 通过分享外部文章链接，gruez 和 mitchbob 提供了更多关于金融行业批评的参考资料，支持了 jmogly 的观点，但没有直接参与讨论。
• jmogly 的个人经历和反思揭示了金融从业者在追求财富过程中可能面临的道德困境和价值迷失，这是整个讨论的核心议题。

data.title: Writing a Game Boy Emulator in OCaml (2022)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者使用OCaml编写Game Boy模拟器（CAMLBOY）的经历和过程。该项目旨在帮助作者克服在学习OCaml过程中遇到的实践难题，并通过一个中型项目深入理解OCaml的高级特性。CAMLBOY模拟器可以在浏览器中运行，支持60 FPS，兼容移动设备。

文章主要内容包括：
1. **项目背景和目标**：通过实现Game Boy模拟器来提升OCaml编程能力，强调代码可读性和可维护性，并编译为JavaScript在浏览器中运行。
2. **Game Boy架构概述**：介绍了CPU、定时器、GPU等核心组件的协同工作机制，以及如何通过主循环实现硬件同步。
3. **代码结构与性能优化**：讲解了如何使用OCaml的函子、GADT和一级模块等高级特性，以及如何识别和优化性能瓶颈。

本文适合对Game Boy模拟器开发或OCaml中型项目实践感兴趣的读者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言与仿真器开发的关系，特别是在学习和教学体验方面的影响；以及与具体技术实现相关的问题。

不同观点：
• [derefr] 认为某些编程语言可能在仿真器、虚拟机、字节码解释器等的开发过程中提供更具回报、更直观的学习体验。他以Erlang在分布式系统中的设计为例，探讨是否存在一种语言在"用代码描述机器"方面具有类似的独特优势，从而帮助开发者更好地理解仿真器和语言本身。
• [le-mark] 对OCaml语言及Gameboy仿真器的实现表示赞赏，并提出创建一个浏览器内组装编辑器和相关工具的设想，认为这将是一个很好的嵌入式开发教学机会，但没有直接回应是否存在特定语言更适合仿真器开发的问题。

补充讨论：
• [droolboy] 提出了一个具体的技术问题，询问是否有关于Game Boy仿真器声音部分的教程。他表示现有教程通常忽略这一部分，且自己尝试实现时遇到困难。
• [mtlynch] 对项目表示赞赏，但提出更新需求（添加2022年的信息）。
• [numlock86] 反馈了仿真器运行速度过快的问题，特别是与帧率和节流设置相关的一个技术问题，指出即使勾选了节流选项，运行速度依然过高。
• [brunojppb] 表示受到启发，计划用Rust编写Game Boy仿真器，表明Rust可能也是一个适合仿真器开发的语言选择。
• [noobcoder] 讨论了使用OCaml中的高级特性（如函子、GADT）以及将相关项目移植到WebAssembly的可能性，提供了具体的比较对象（CHIP-8或NES仿真器）。

争议焦点：
• 是否存在一种编程语言，其设计特别适合于仿真器开发，能够提供更具教学意义的开发体验，这一点在[derefr]的提问中被提出，但未有明确答案，讨论者更多关注具体的技术问题和个人项目经验。

Contents
Writing a Game Boy Emulator in OCaml
linoscope
2022-01-11
5872 words
28 minutes
Contents
Introduction
For the past few months, I have been working on a project called
CAMLBOY
, a Game Boy emulator written in OCaml that runs in the browser. You can try it out on the following demo page:
Demo Page
I included several homebrew ROMs in the demo, so please try them out (I recommend
Bouncing ball
and
Rocket Man Demo
). You can also play with it in your mobile browser as it runs at 60 FPS on recent smartphones.
Repository
You can find the repository here:
https://github.com/linoscope/CAMLBOY
Star
Fork
Screenshots
Why implement a Game Boy emulator in OCaml?
Have you ever felt like the following when learning a new programming language?
You can write simple program snippets but
you don’t know how to write medium/large scale code
1
.
You have studied
advanced language features
2
and have a rough understanding of how they work, but
you don’t know how to use them in practice
.
These were exactly my thoughts when I started to study OCaml seriously a few months ago. I understood the basics of the language by reading books and implementing simple algorithms, but the above two “don’t know"s prevented me from feeling like I could
really
write OCaml. I knew that the only way to get out of this situation was practice, so I started looking for a project to work on.
I choose a Game Boy emulator as the project for the following reasons:
It has clear specifications, so there is no need to think about what to implement.
It is complex enough that it cannot be completed in a few days or weeks.
It is not so complex that it can’t be completed in a few months.
I have fond childhood memories of playing the Game Boy.
I set the following goals for the emulator:
Write code with an emphasis on readability and maintainability.
Compile to JavaScript using
js_of_ocaml
and run it in the browser.
Achieve playable FPS in the smartphone browser.
Implement some benchmarks and compare various compiler backends
3
.
Goal of this article
This article aims to take you through the journey of creating a Game Boy emulator in OCaml.
This article is for you if you are interested in what it is like to
Implement a Game Boy emulator.
Implement a middle-scale project in OCaml.
Use advanced features of OCaml in practice.
We will cover things like
Overview of the Game Boy architecture.
How to structure your code in a testable and reusable way.
How to use functors, GADTs, and first-class modules in practice.
How to find bottlenecks and improve performance.
General thoughts on OCaml.
We will not cover things like
Basic OCaml syntax.
Details of the Game Boy architecture.
You can find materials about these uncovered topics in the
Recommended Materials
section.
Implementation
Architecture diagram
A schematic diagram of CAMLBOY looks like this:
4
I’ll explain the details as needed, but in a nutshell:
The CPU/timer/GPU operates at a fixed rate according to a clock.
The bus sits between the CPU and various hardware modules and routes data reads/writes based on the given address. For example, writes to address
0xFFFF
is routed to the interrupt controller and enables/disables interrupts based on the written value.
Hardware modules connected to the bus implement the interface
Addressable_intf.S
(which I will explain later)
The bus implements the interface
Word_addressable_intf.S
(which I will explain later)
There are various types of cartridges.
The timer, GPU, serial port, and joypad can request interrupts. The interrupt controller will notify the requested interrupt to the CPU (further explanation of interrupts is omitted in this article).
Main loop
The main loop is responsible for progressing the clocked hardware modules (highlighted in red below) in a synchronized way.
In real hardware, the CPU/timer/GPU share the same hardware clock, so they naturally run in a synchronized state. On the other hand, the emulator is just a sequential execution loop, so we need to devise a way to reproduce the synchronization between these components. To do so, I implemented the main loop to contain the following steps:
Let the CPU execute one instruction and keep track of the number of cycles consumed as a result.
Advance the timer by the number of cycles consumed by the CPU.
Advance the GPU by the number of cycles consumed by the CPU.
We sometimes call this the
catch up method
because it makes the timer and GPU “catch up” with the CPU. Here is the implementation:

run_instruction
t
=
let
mcycles
=
Cpu

t

cpu

t

~
mcycles

t

~
mcycles
Interface for reading/writing data
We will look at some basic interfaces used throughout the emulator.
Interface for reading/writing 8-bit data
First, let’s look at the interface for reading/writing 8-bit data used in the red line below.

data.title: US plans to shut down Mauna Loa Observatory
data.author: OutOfHere
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了美国计划关闭莫纳罗亚天文台及其对气候变化监测的影响。自1958年以来，该天文台通过基林曲线记录了大气中二氧化碳（CO₂）水平的持续上升，首次清晰展示了人类活动对气候的显著影响。数据显示，CO₂水平已从1960年代的约320 ppm上升到现在的超过420 ppm，达到了三百万年来的最高水平。这种快速增长主要源于燃烧化石燃料。莫纳罗亚的数据对于验证气候政策的效果至关重要。若该天文台关闭，将对气候科学造成重大损失，其他观测站如澳大利亚的Kennaook/Cape Grim将变得更加重要。持续监测CO₂水平对于应对气候变化至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国当前形势及其未来

不同观点：
• java-man认为美国正在逐渐被摧毁，且这种趋势无法逆转，直到国家陷入如同1945年德国和日本般的 ruin（毁灭）。这一观点带有较强的悲观色彩，并将美国当前的局势类比为二战后彻底破坏的国家。

July 5, 2025
The GIST
Mauna Loa Observatory captured the reality of climate change: The US plans to shut it down
by Alex Sen Gupta, Katrin Meissner, Timothy H. Raupach,
The Conversation
edited by
Sadie Harley
, 																								reviewed by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
written by researcher(s)
proofread
Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain
The greenhouse effect was discovered more than 150 years ago and the first scientific paper linking carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere with climate change was published
in 1896
.
But it wasn't until the 1950s that scientists could definitively detect the effect of human activities on the Earth's atmosphere.
In 1956, United States scientist Charles Keeling chose Hawaii's Mauna Loa volcano as the site of a new atmospheric measuring station. It was ideal, located in the middle of the Pacific Ocean and at
high altitude
away from the confounding influence of population centers.
Data collected by Mauna Loa from 1958 onwards let us clearly see the evidence of climate change for the first time. The station samples the air and measures global CO₂ levels. Charles Keeling and his successors used this data to produce the famous
Keeling curve
—a graph showing carbon dioxide levels increasing year after year.
But this precious record is in peril. US President Donald Trump
has decided
to
defund the observatory
recording the data, as well as the widespread US greenhouse gas monitoring network and other climate measuring sites.
We can't solve the existential problem of
climate change
if we can't track the changes. Losing Mauna Loa would be a huge loss to climate science. If it shuts, other observatories such as Australia's
Kennaook/Cape Grim
will become even more vital.
What did Mauna Loa show us?
The first year of measurements at Mauna Loa revealed something incredible. For the first time, the clear annual cycle in atmospheric CO₂ was visible. As plants grow in summer, they absorb CO₂ and draw it out of the atmosphere. As they die and decay in winter, the CO₂ returns to the atmosphere. It's like Earth is breathing.
Most land on Earth is in the Northern Hemisphere, which means this cycle is largely influenced by the northern summer and winter.
It only took a few years of measurements before an even more profound pattern emerged.
Year on year, CO
2
levels in the atmosphere were relentlessly rising. The natural in-out cycle continued, but against a steady increase.
Scientists would later figure out that the ocean and land together were absorbing almost half of the CO
2
produced by humans. But the rest was building up in the atmosphere.
Crucially, isotopic measurements meant scientists could be crystal clear about the origin of the extra carbon dioxide. It was coming from humans, largely through burning fossil fuels.
Mauna Loa has now been collecting data for more than 65 years. The resulting Keeling curve graph is the most iconic demonstration of how human activities are collectively affecting the planet.
When the last of the Baby Boomer generation were being born in the 1960s, CO
2
levels were around 320 parts per million. Now they're over 420 ppm. That's a level unseen for at least
three million years
. The rate of increase
far exceeds
any natural change in the past 50 million years.
The reason carbon dioxide is so important is that this molecule has special properties. Its ability to trap heat alongside other
greenhouse gases
means Earth isn't a frozen rock. If there were no greenhouse gases, Earth would have an average temperature of -18°C, rather than the balmy 14°C under which human civilization emerged.
The
greenhouse effect
is essential to life. But if there are too many gases, the planet becomes dangerously hot. That's what's happening now—a very sharp increase in gases exceptionally good at trapping heat even at low concentrations.

100,000 subscribers
who rely on Phys.org for daily insights.
Sign up for our
free newsletter
and get updates on breakthroughs,
innovations, and research that matter—
daily or weekly
.
Subscribe
Keeping our eyes open
It's not enough to know CO
2
is climbing. Monitoring is essential. That's because as the planet warms, both the ocean and the land are expected to take up less and less of humanity's emissions, letting still more carbon accumulate in the air.
Continuous, high-precision monitoring is the only way to spot if and when that happens.
This monitoring provides the vital means to verify whether new climate policies are genuinely influencing the atmospheric CO
2
curve rather than just being touted as effective. Monitoring will also be vital to capture the moment many have been working towards when
government policies
and new technologies finally slow and eventually stop the increas

data.article_summary: 《Tower of Time》是一款为2025年夏季游戏开发赛制作的塔防游戏，玩家通过时间倒流机制在敌人攻势下调整策略。游戏特色包括多种防御塔、能量管理系统和基于波次的敌人生成。时间倒流功能允许玩家在失败时重设策略，游戏支持键盘和手柄操作。该项目约95%的代码由AI辅助完成，使用Phaser 3引擎和TypeScript语言，通过Vite构建工具管理项目。开发过程中，作者认识到AI能加速原型设计，但需谨慎过渡到最终游戏，且代码量可进一步优化。项目依据MIT许可证开源，并在itch.io平台提供试玩。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在代码开发中的应用及其实际效果

不同观点：
• **twalkz** 认为，AI编码成功的关键在于将复杂的项目分解为数百个小问题，并针对关键部分进行具体的架构指导，而不是依赖简单的“氛围编码”（vibe coding）。他强调了细致规划和明确想法的重要性。
• **mgdev** 支持AI编码的应用，并指出AI工具的杠杆效应与指令质量和交互结构成正比。他还提到，AI可以帮助澄清思维和教学，但目前仍需要人工的参与来校正输出和指导方向。
• **SquibblesRedux** 质疑AI生成代码是否真的是“AI”，还是只是一种新的搜索形式，特别是在有大量现有代码示例的情况下。
• **alganet** 关注代码生成的过程，特别是AI是否完全从零开始生成某些代码文件，并希望了解更多关于代码历史的细节。

补充讨论：
• **Brajeshwar** 分享了自己使用AI辅助编码的经历，虽然结果有限（如泡泡包装爆破器和消音器），但承认AI在某些情况下可以提供帮助。
• **doddpronter** 认为“氛围编码”可以加速开发过程，但前提是需要清晰简洁的指令和快速审查代码的能力。
• **skybrian** 对Augment Code工具提出了基本的问题，如其功能、选择理由及使用效果，显示出对新工具的兴趣和谨慎态度。
• **Lerc** 讨论了AI在游戏设计中的潜在应用，特别是如何让AI“感受”游戏动态，并提出了将游戏状态编码为标记的设想。
• **colinmilhaupt** 强调了在LLM增强的工作流中引入可追溯性和透明性的重要性，认为共享和提交提示可以提供更多开发过程的洞察。
• **shironandonon_** 分享了自己与Gemini-cli配合进行编码的积极经验，特别是通过明确提示和分块解决问题所获得的良好结果。
• **davidmurdoch** 描述了使用AI编写大量代码的有趣经历，指出了AI编写代码的冗长和某些不必要的防护措施，但总体上认为AI是有趣且有用的工具。
• **freehorse** 报告了游戏中的一个具体bug，提供了关于游戏体验的反馈。
• **edgarneto** 赞赏游戏的创意，并建议将游戏发布到Reddit上，利用用户生成内容（UGC）来增加游戏的趣味性。
• **iaw** 认为AI开发技术的潜力尚未完全释放，显示出对未来发展的期待。
• **adelineJoOs** 对开发过程的透明性和共享提示表示赞赏，并对游戏表示了喜爱。

争议焦点：
• AI生成代码是否应被视为真正的“AI”应用，还是仅仅是现有代码的搜索和重组。
• AI在编码中能多大程度上替代人工，特别是在复杂项目和高品质软件开发中的角色。

Tower of Time
Entry for Beginner's Jam Summer 2025
A time-traveling tower defense game where you defend your base against waves of enemies using the power to rewind time.
🎮 Play the game at https://m4v3k.itch.io/tower-of-time
About the game
Tower of Time is a unique tower defense game that combines strategic building with time manipulation mechanics. When enemies overwhelm your defenses, use your time-travel powers to rewind and rebuild your strategy. The game features multiple tower types, energy management, and wave-based enemy spawning.
Key Features
Time Rewind
: Roll back time to survive the enemy waves
Multiple Tower Types
: Basic turrets, sniper towers, slowdown towers, and splash damage towers
Energy System
: Manage energy for building towers and rewinding time
Controls
Game supports both keyboard and gamepad.
Move
: Arrow Keys / Gamepad Analog Stick
Action
: Spacebar / Cross (PlayStation) / A (Xbox)
Rewind
: Backspace / Left Trigger
Vibe Coding Proof of Concept
This game serves as a proof of concept for AI-assisted game development. Approximately 95% of the codebase was written by AI using:
Augment Code
- Advanced codebase context and AI coding assistance
Cursor
- AI-powered code editor, mostly using Agent mode
Claude Sonnet 4
- My LLM of choice for this project (also used OpenAI o3 and Claude Opus 4 occasionally)
For detailed prompts and development process, see
PROMPTS.md
.
What I've learned:
It is entirely possible to develop a game with AI, but you need to know what you're doing
AI makes prototyping super fast, but as you transition from prototype to final game you need to be careful
AIs like to write
a lot
of code, this project could probably have two times less code
Claude Sonnet 4 knows Phaser.js pretty well but for key areas I've given it a URL to the docs for the specific feature I was working on and it helped
If the AI gets stuck on something ask it to add debug/console logs and share them with the agent
If after that it still gets stuck don't fight it, roll back everything and try rephrasing the prompt or giving it more context

data.title: LooksMapping
data.author: elsewhen
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由walzr.com创建的项目，通过人工智能（AI）分析数百万Google Maps餐厅评论中的用户头像，并根据吸引力进行打分（从1到10）。该项目制作了一张地图，显示每个餐厅顾客的吸引力，红色代表高，蓝色代表低。文章承认该模型存在偏见和缺陷，但指出人们常常根据顾客来判断餐厅，这一项目只是将日常的表面判断数字化，反映了人们的集体虚荣心。目前该地图可用于纽约、洛杉矶和旧金山。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成餐厅推荐的有效性及潜在偏见

不同观点：
• **支持技术创新和娱乐价值**：
   - [donatj] 认为这是现代技术驱动的有趣内容，表示希望看到更多类似的项目。
   - [getcrunk] 赞赏这种新颖的创意，并对背后的技术实现感兴趣，询问了数据抓取的技术细节。
   - [bemmu] 指出这种AI应用解决了一些人类不愿意或无法高效完成的任务，认为这种项目有一定的实用性和娱乐价值。
   - [1GZ0] 认为人们因为项目的前提不够得体就 dismiss 了背后的技术能力，表达了对技术创新的支持。

• **质疑和批评偏见问题**：
   - [cobertos] 质疑人们是否真的会依据顾客来判断餐厅，并表示这从未影响他的饮食习惯。
   - [defyonce] 通过对比男女餐厅偏好列表，暗示女性偏好的餐厅更加“吸引人”，而男性偏好的餐厅评分较低，引发了对性别偏见的讨论。
   - [xg15] 指出AI模型在哈莱姆地区表现出潜在的种族和阶级偏见，认为该模型无意中暴露了社会不平等问题。
   - [pimlottc] 直接表示该项目在多个层面上令人不适。
   - [Eduard] 提到AI模型存在对美丽标准的偏见，指出当顾客是黑人或亚洲人时，热度排名会下降。
   - [Mashimo] 提到洛杉矶的餐厅被标记为老年人聚集地，质疑AI是否能正确识别年龄，并暗示可能存在种族偏见。
   - [d--b] 最初觉得网站有趣，但在发现哈莱姆地区餐厅评分偏低后感到不满。

• **幽默和无关评价**：
   - [TheLockranore] 认为这像90年代浪漫喜剧的开场前提。
   - [jofzar] 将该项目比作老派网络内容，带有幽默感。
   - [esafak] 以幽默方式建议在纽约应改为“热狗摊”排名。

补充讨论：
- 偏见问题：多个评论提到AI模型中的种族、年龄和性别偏见，特别是哈莱姆地区餐厅的低评分引发了对模型公正性的关注。
- 技术实现：部分评论对项目的技术实现表现出浓厚兴趣，关注如何实现数据抓取和AI模型的运作原理。
- 娱乐与实用性：一些评论认为该项目尽管带有娱乐性质，但确实提出了一些有趣的技术挑战，并展示了AI在特定场景下的应用潜力。

44461015.article_content:
See Which Restaurants Have The Most Attractive Diners –
According to AI!
Search
I scraped millions of Google Maps restaurant reviews, and gave each reviewer's profile picture to an AI model that rates how hot they are out of 10. This map shows how attractive each restaurant's clientele is. Red means hot, blue means not.
The model is certainly biased. It's certainly flawed. But we judge places by the people who go there. We always have. And
are we not also flawed?
This website just puts reductive numbers on the superficial calculations we make every day. A mirror held up to our collective vanity.

data.title: Introducing tmux-rs
data.author: Jtsummers
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者将tmux从C语言移植到Rust的过程，历时六个月，最近实现了代码库100%由Rust编写。作者解释了重写tmux的原因仅是将其作为个人爱好项目，类似于园艺，但伴随着更多的段错误。最初，作者使用了C2Rust工具自动转换代码，但生成的Rust代码难以维护，体积是原C代码的三倍。作者随后放弃自动转换，选择手动翻译代码。尽管如此，作者仍肯定了C2Rust工具的价值，因为它帮助项目从一开始就可编译运行。文章还介绍了构建过程，包括从原始的Makefile到Rust的Cargo构建系统的转换，并详细描述了开发中遇到的一些有趣的bug和挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust重写tmux项目的价值与技术挑战

不同观点：
• [starchild3001] 认为该项目展示了现代基础设施代码更新中的实际挑战，对作者的手动移植决策表示赞同，并指出自动代码翻译工具在保持代码习惯用法方面的不足。他还对从`unsafe` Rust转换为安全Rust的策略表示关注，特别是如何处理原始指针和复杂控制流。
• [ethagnawl] 对将rmuxinator与tmux-rs集成的可能性表示兴趣，并提出两种技术方案：将rmuxinator作为依赖项引入tmux-rs，或反过来使用tmux-rs管理会话。他计划在修复当前bug后尝试这些方案。
• [mbreese] 赞赏作者的态度，认为无需为新项目寻找理由，并将编码项目与园艺相比，认为编码更安全。
• [tekawade] 表达了对Rust解决方案的热爱，并推荐了另一个Rust编写的终端复用器zellij，但也指出zellij缺少一些tmux具备的功能。
• [gmoque] 强调项目的过程比结果更重要，认为即使是重写成熟应用，也能带来很多学习机会，并建议通过修复bug和优化代码吸引Rust初学者参与。
• [usrbinbash] 对项目的实用性提出质疑，认为Rust在tmux这样的应用中相较于C并没有明显的内存安全性优势，且代码库变大。他建议使用Go语言重写tmux，认为Go更适合这类应用。

补充讨论：
• [pizlonator] 提到将tmux移植到Fil-C语言，声称实现了完全内存安全，且用时不到一小时。
• [tialaramex] 分享了关于Rust命令行工具的视频资源，认为对Rust开发者和其他命令行用户都有帮助。
• [someperson] 建议改进c2rust工具，以减少翻译过程中信息的丢失，降低初始转换的负担。
• [rthnbgrredf] 认为未来大型语言模型有可能实现C代码到安全Rust的高效自动翻译，但目前技术尚未成熟。
• [xvilka] 对zellij的功能不足表示失望，特别提到状态栏显示问题。
• [teekert] 对tmux的用户体验提出改进建议，如滚轮滚动和快捷键切换窗格。

争议焦点：
• 重写tmux为Rust项目的实际价值，特别是在性能和代码大小方面的优势受到质疑（[usrbinbash]的观点）。
• 自动代码翻译工具的有效性和在保持代码习惯用法方面的局限性（[starchild3001]与[rthnbgrredf]的讨论）。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对Rust生态系统中不同终端复用器（如zellij和tmux-rs）的功能比较和集成可能性（[tekawade]和[ethagnawl]的观点）。
• 项目过程中遇到的实际技术问题和调试经验，如FFI问题和结构布局不匹配（[starchild3001]的具体例子）。

3 July 2025
Introducing tmux-rs
by Collin Richards
For the 6 months or so I’ve been quietly porting tmux from C to Rust. I’ve recently reached a big milestone: the code base is now 100% (unsafe) Rust.
I’d like to share the process of porting the original codebase from ~67,000 lines of C code to ~81,000 lines of Rust (excluding comments and empty lines).
You might be asking: why did you rewrite tmux in Rust? And yeah, I don’t really have a good reason. It’s a hobby project. Like gardening, but with more segfaults.

COLOUR_FLAG_256
which is translated to
0x1000000
. There are also a lot of casts to
libc::c_int
polluting the code as well. I suspect this is to handle
C’s integer promotion rules
. Most of them are completely unnecessary when doing operations on literals in Rust.
I spent quite a lot of time manually refactoring the shitty Rust code to less shitty Rust code, but I kept finding myself having to look at the original C code to understand the program’s intent. After manually refactoring many files this way I gave up on this approach. I threw away all of the C2Rust output and decided I would translate all of the files into Rust manually from C.
Despite not using C2Rust for this project I still think it’s a great tool. It was very important for me to actually be able to compile and run the project from the start. It made me realize this endeavour was achievable. I’ve even integrated it as part of one of my
other side projects
.

44455787.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者将tmux从C语言移植到Rust的过程，历时六个月，最近实现了代码库100%由Rust编写。作者解释了重写tmux的原因仅是将其作为个人爱好项目，类似于园艺，但伴随着更多的段错误。最初，作者使用了C2Rust工具自动转换代码，但生成的Rust代码难以维护，体积是原C代码的三倍。作者随后放弃自动转换，选择手动翻译代码。尽管如此，作者仍肯定了C2Rust工具的价值，因为它帮助项目从一开始就可编译运行。文章还介绍了构建过程，包括从原始的Makefile到Rust的Cargo构建系统的转换，并详细描述了开发中遇到的一些有趣的bug和挑战。

data.article_summary: Larry是自2011年起担任英国首相官邸首席捕鼠官的家猫，出生于2007年1月，原为流浪猫，后由巴特西猫狗之家收养。2011年，他被引入唐宁街10号，为时任首相卡梅伦的孩子们所养。尽管他被描述为“捕鼠高手”，但也有报道称他缺乏“杀手本能”，更多时间用于睡觉而非捕鼠，因此被戏称为“懒惰拉里”。他的职位由唐宁街工作人员自愿资助，不属于英国政府开支。拉里经历了多任首相，包括卡梅伦、特蕾莎·梅、约翰逊、特拉斯、苏纳克和斯塔默。2023年有报道称拉里健康状况不佳，但唐宁街予以否认，称其“快乐健康”。拉里在公众中享有较高支持率，甚至超过一些政界人物。

Larry
(born
c.
January 2007
) is a British domestic
tabby cat
who has served as
Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office
at
10 Downing Street
since 2011. He is cared for by Downing Street staff, and is not the personal property of the
prime minister of the United Kingdom
. Larry has lived at 10 Downing Street during the premierships of six prime ministers:
David Cameron
,
Theresa May
,
Boris Johnson
,
Liz Truss
,
Rishi Sunak
and
Keir Starmer
. He is the first cat to be officially given the title of Chief Mouser, according to the Downing Street government website.
[
1
]
Early life
[
edit
]
Larry was born as a
stray cat
around January 2007 and later came into the possession of
Battersea Dogs & Cats Home
. In 2011 he was adopted by Downing Street staff, initially intended to be a pet for Cameron’s children.
[
2
]
He was described by Downing Street sources as a "good ratter" and as having "a high chase-drive and hunting instinct".
[
3
]
In 2012 the Home said Larry's publicity had resulted in a 15% increase in cat adoptions.
[
4
]
Soon after he was taken in at Downing Street, a story circulated in the press purporting that Larry was a lost cat and that the original owner had begun a campaign to retrieve him.
[
5
]
However, it was later found to be a hoax, and neither the owner nor the campaign existed.
[
6
]
Career
[
edit
]
Official duties
[
edit
]
The Downing Street website describes Larry's duties as "greeting guests to the house, inspecting security defences and testing antique furniture for napping quality". It says he is "contemplating a solution to the mouse occupancy of the house" and has told Downing Street that such a solution is still in the "tactical planning stage".
[
1
]
Unlike his predecessors since 1929, Larry's costs are funded voluntarily by members of staff, at no cost to
His Majesty's Government
.
[
7
]
[
8
]
Fundraising events (organised to pay for his food) are believed to have included a quiz night, held in the state rooms.
[
9
]
David Cameron explained during his final
Prime Minister's Questions
in 2016 that Larry is a
civil servant
and not his personal property, and would therefore stay at Downing Street after his successor took office.
[
10
]
Larry has maintained his position through the
May
,
Johnson
,
Truss
,
Sunak
and
Starmer
ministries.
Work as chief mouser
[
edit
]
Within a month of his arrival at Downing Street, anonymous sources described Larry as having "a distinct lack of killer instinct."
[
11
]
Later that year, it was revealed that Larry spent more time sleeping than hunting for mice, and shared the company of a female cat, Maisie.
[
12
]
At one point in 2011, mice were so endemic in Downing Street that the Prime Minister, David Cameron, resorted to throwing a fork at one during a Cabinet dinner.
[
12
]
His lack of killer instinct also earned him the nickname "Lazy Larry" by the tabloid press.
[
13
]
He made his first known kill, a mouse, on 22 April 2011.
[
14
]
On 28 August 2012 Larry made his first public killing, dropping his prey on the lawn in front of Number 10.
[
15
]
In September 2012
Freya
was also appointed the role of Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office. In October 2013 Larry caught four mice in two weeks and one staff member rescued a mouse from his clutches.
[
16
]
In July 2015,
George Osborne
, the
chancellor of the exchequer
, and Cabinet Office minister
Matt Hancock
, the
minister for the Cabinet Office
, cornered a mouse in the Chancellor's office, trapping it in a brown paper sandwich bag. The press joked that Osborne might take over the position of Chief Mouser.
[
17
]
Health
[
edit
]
In September 2023
The Sun
reported that Larry had been in ill health for some time and that Downing Street staff were preparing for his death.
[
18
]
A statement from Downing Street denied this and described Larry as "happy and healthy."
[
19
]
In August 2024 it was reported staff at Downing Street had begun preparing plans for how to announce Larry’s death to the public. It was however stated Larry was still doing just fine.
[
20
]
Public image
[
edit
]
Ahead of the
2024 general election
, an opinion poll from
Ipsos
showed that Larry had a higher favourability rating (44%) and net favourability rating (40%) than both Sunak (22% and –36%) and Starmer (34% and –7%).

21
]
Relationships with politicians
[
edit
]
Larry with Prime Minister
David Cameron
and US President
Barack Obama

data.title: Context Engineering for Agents
data.author: 0x79de
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在开发大型语言模型（LLM）应用时，上下文工程（context engineering）的重要性，特别是在处理长时任务和工具调用时的策略。LLM的上下文窗口类似于计算机的RAM，容量有限，需精心管理以确保有效性能。文中提到四种需管理的上下文类型：指令、知识和工具。随着智能体（agents）在推理和工具调用方面的进步，管理长时间对话和反馈成为关键挑战，可能导致上下文中毒、分心、混淆和冲突等问题。

为应对这些挑战，作者提出了四种策略：
1. **写入上下文**：将信息保存在上下文窗口之外，如使用“草稿纸”（scratchpad）存储任务计划。
2. **选择上下文**：从草稿纸或运行时状态中选择相关信息供智能体使用。
3. **压缩上下文**：通过摘要或精简方式减少上下文大小。
